mainTopic: When ספירת העומר begins and how it is done, which proofs for the 16th of ניסן stand, and how the עומר was prepared.
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא that brings proofs against the בייתוסים, who read ״מִמָּחֳרַת הַשַּׁבָּת״ as the Sunday after a regular שבת. One proof uses ״תִּסְפׇּר לָךְ״, which ties the count to the בית דין. רבי יוסי gives two more proofs, and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר settles the clash between six and seven days of מצה. All of them show that the עומר is brought on the 16th of ניסן. The ברייתא then works out the timing: the harvesting and the counting are done at night, and the עומר is brought in the day. רבא then judges all the proofs. He shows how most of them can be pushed off, and only the last two תנאים in each ברייתא stand. The גמרא then looks at אביי's rule that we count both days and weeks, and reports that אמימר counted only days, since today the count is a זכר למקדש. A new משנה describes how the עומר was parched, ground, and sifted, and what happens to the leftover flour. The גמרא begins with a ברייתא on ״קָלוּי בָּאֵשׁ״, and the חכמים' reading of it continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The counting depends on the court, so it cannot start from a weekly שבת
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends a proof from the words ״תִּסְפׇּר לָךְ״. The counting is tied to the בית דין, so it cannot be counted from שבת בראשית, which anyone can count.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says ״you shall count for you.″ This shows the counting depends on the court. That rules out the weekly שבת, since every person can count to it on his own.
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of a ברייתא that proves ״מִמָּחֳרַת הַשַּׁבָּת״ means the day after יום טוב. This line finishes one of those proofs, using the words ״תִּסְפׇּר לָךְ״.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The date of יום טוב depends on when the בית דין declared ראש חודש, so only they know when פסח falls. A weekly שבת comes every seven days, and anyone can track it without the court. Since the פסוק links the counting to the court, the starting point must be יום טוב and not a weekly שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: Counting. Here it means counting the days of the עומר.
Depends on the court, which sets the calendar by declaring ראש חודש.
The regular weekly שבת, which goes back to Creation.
It is excluded, meaning this possibility is ruled out.

phrases.english: Behold it says: "You shall count for you,"
phrases.notes: דברים 16:9

phrases.english: the counting depends on the court,
which excludes the Shabbat of Creation,
whose counting is done by every person.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲרֵי הוּא אוֹמֵר: ״תִּסְפׇּר לָךְ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues a proof begun earlier in the ברייתא, before this section.
steps.raayaObject: That the count begins from יום טוב and not from a weekly שבת.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The words ״תִּסְפׇּר לָךְ״ (דברים 16:9), read as tying the count to the בית דין.

steps.title: רבי יוסי: ״מִמָּחֳרַת הַשַּׁבָּת״ means the day after יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי states that ״מִמָּחֳרַת הַשַּׁבָּת״ means the day after יום טוב of פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי says: "From the day after the שבת" means from the day after the holiday.
steps.whatsHappening: A new תנא, רבי יוסי, gives his reading of the פסוק. The next steps will prove it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי reads the word ״שַּׁבָּת״ here as a day of rest in general, namely the first day of פסח. That would make the count start on the 16th of ניסן every year, no matter what day of the week it is.

keyTerms.meaning: From the day after the day of rest (ויקרא 23:15).
A holiday, here the first day of פסח.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei says:
"From the morrow after the Shabbat" means from the morrow after the Festival.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:15

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another תנא brings his own proof for the same conclusion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ״השבת״ in this פסוק means יום טוב, so the count starts the day after the first day of פסח.

steps.title: Maybe it means the day after a regular weekly שבת?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא raises the other possible reading: maybe ״השבת״ really means the weekly שבת, and the count starts on Sunday.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say it means the day after the holiday? Or maybe it only means the day after the weekly שבת?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises the opposite reading so that it can knock it down. This sets up רבי יוסי's proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain meaning of the word שבת is the weekly שבת, so the question is a fair one. Answering it is what makes רבי יוסי's reading convincing.

keyTerms.meaning: "Do you say... or is it only...?" This is a standard way of raising another possible reading of a פסוק.

phrases.english: Do you say from the morrow after the Festival,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא מִמָּחֳרַת שַׁבַּת בְּרֵאשִׁית?
phrases.english: or is it only from the morrow after the Shabbat of Creation?
phrases.notes: In other words, the Sunday after the weekly שבת.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר מִמָּחֳרַת יוֹם טוֹב, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא מִמָּחֳרַת שַׁבַּת בְּרֵאשִׁית
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises the other possible reading of רבי יוסי's פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether ״השבת״ could mean the weekly שבת instead of יום טוב.

steps.title: The תורה never said which שבת, so it cannot mean a weekly שבת
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק does not say "the שבת during פסח." Since the year has many שבתות, a plain ״השבת״ would leave us not knowing which one. So it must mean יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can answer: does the פסוק say "the day after the שבת that falls during פסח"? It only says "the day after the שבת." The whole year is full of שבתות, so go figure out which שבת it means!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי answers the question. If the פסוק meant a weekly שבת, it would have had to say which one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are about fifty weekly שבתות in a year, and the פסוק gives no clue which one it means. A specific יום טוב, however, is already clear from the context of פסח. So ״השבת״ has to be the first day of פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: "Is it then written...?" This is a question that expects the answer no.
Full of שבתות.
"Go out and check." Here it means you would have no way to know.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the first of רבי יוסי's two proofs. Later (step 22) רבא says רבי יוסי himself saw a weakness in it, which is why he added a second proof with ״וְעוֹד״.

phrases.english: You can say: Is it then stated:
"From the morrow after the Shabbat that is during Passover"?
Rather, it is stated only: "From the morrow after the Shabbat,"
and the entire year is full of Shabbatot,
so go and check which Shabbat it is.
phrases.notes: There is no way to tell which one. So it must be a שבת we already know about, the first day of פסח.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַרְתָּ: וְכִי נֶאֱמַר ״מִמָּחֳרַת הַשַּׁבָּת שֶׁבְּתוֹךְ הַפֶּסַח״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק does not say which weekly שבת it means, so it must mean the one known day, יום טוב.

steps.title: A second proof: the word שבת in the שבועות פסוק means a יום טוב
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי compares the word שבת here to the word שבת said about שבועות. There it refers to a holiday, so here too it means a holiday.
steps.simpleTranslation: Also, the word ״שבת״ is said below, and the word ״שבת״ is said above. Just as there it is about a holiday and the start of a holiday, so too here it is about a holiday and the start of a holiday.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוסי adds a second proof by comparing two places where the word שבת appears.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word שבת appears both where the count starts and where it ends at שבועות. In the שבועות פסוק it is tied to a holiday and its start. Using the same word teaches that here too, ״השבת״ means a holiday: the start of פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: "And furthermore." It introduces another proof.
Below and above, meaning a later פסוק and an earlier פסוק.
A Festival, one of the pilgrimage holidays.
"Just as there... so too here." A comparison that carries a meaning from one place to another.

phrases.english: And furthermore, "Shabbat" is stated below,
phrases.notes: "Below" is ויקרא 23:16, about counting until שבועות.

phrases.english: and "Shabbat" is stated above.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:15, where the counting begins.

phrases.english: Just as there it refers to a Festival and the beginning of a Festival,
so too here it refers to a Festival and the beginning of a Festival.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד, נֶאֶמְרָה ״שַׁבָּת״ לְמַטָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second proof for רבי יוסי's reading.
steps.raayaObject: That ״השבת״ means יום טוב of פסח.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The same word שבת used in the שבועות פסוק, where it refers to a holiday.

steps.title: Two פסוקים clash: six days of מצה or seven?
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר points out that one פסוק says to eat מצה for six days and another says seven, and asks how both can be true.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says: one פסוק says "Six days you shall eat מצות," and another פסוק says "Seven days you shall eat מצות." How can that be?
steps.whatsHappening: A third תנא sets up his proof by pointing out two פסוקים that seem to contradict each other. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים are about eating מצה on פסח, yet they give different numbers. The way he settles the clash will show us when the עומר is brought.

keyTerms.term: כָּתוּב אֶחָד אוֹמֵר... וְכָתוּב אֶחָד אוֹמֵר
keyTerms.meaning: "One פסוק says... and another פסוק says..." This is how two clashing פסוקים are introduced.
"How can this be?" It asks how the two פסוקים fit together.
Unleavened bread.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:

phrases.aramaic: כָּתוּב אֶחָד אוֹמֵר: ״שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים תֹּאכַל מַצּוֹת״,
phrases.english: One verse says: "Six days you shall eat unleavened bread,"
phrases.notes: דברים 16:8

phrases.aramaic: וְכָתוּב אֶחָד אוֹמֵר: ״שִׁבְעַת יָמִים מַצּוֹת תֹּאכֵלוּ״.
phrases.english: and one verse says: "Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread."
phrases.notes: שמות 12:15

phrases.english: How is this?

steps.triggerLanguage: כָּתוּב אֶחָד אוֹמֵר: ״שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים תֹּאכַל מַצּוֹת״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new תנא begins a separate proof for the same point.
steps.kashyaTarget: The two פסוקים about how many days מצה is eaten.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One פסוק says six days and the other says seven, so they appear to contradict.

steps.title: מצה from the new grain (חדש) can be eaten for six days, not seven
steps.stepSummary: Seven days refers to מצה in general. Six days refers to מצה from the new crop, which is allowed only after the עומר. This works only if the עומר is always brought on the second day of פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: There is a kind of מצה you cannot eat for seven days, meaning מצה made from the new grain. But you can eat it for six days.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר settles the clash. The six days are the days when מצה from the new grain becomes allowed, after the עומר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: New grain (חדש) is forbidden until the עומר is brought. If the עומר is always brought on the 16th of ניסן, new-grain מצה is allowed for exactly the last six days of פסח. If the עומר were brought on a Sunday that could fall on any day of פסח, the number six would not always be true. So the פסוק proves the עומר is always on the second day of פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: Grain from the new crop, which is forbidden until the עומר is brought.
You are not able, meaning you are not allowed.

steps.whatToRemember: All of these proofs reach the same conclusion: ״מִמָּחֳרַת הַשַּׁבָּת״ means the day after the first day of פסח. So the עומר is brought, and the counting begins, on the 16th of ניסן every year.
steps.confusionAlert: "Six days" does not mean there is no מצוה of מצה on the first day of פסח. It means that מצה from the new grain is allowed only for the six days after the עומר.

phrases.english: Matzah that you are not able to eat
for seven days from the new grain,
phrases.notes: New grain stays forbidden until the עומר is brought on the second day of פסח.

phrases.aramaic: אַתָּה יָכוֹל לְאוֹכְלָהּ שִׁשָּׁה מִן הֶחָדָשׁ.
phrases.english: you are able to eat for six days from the new grain.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַצָּה שֶׁאִי אַתָּה יָכוֹל לְאוֹכְלָהּ שִׁבְעָה מִן הֶחָדָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the clash between the two פסוקים raised in step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each פסוק is talking about something different: seven days for מצה in general, six days for מצה from the new grain.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The two פסוקים seem to give different numbers for the same מצוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Six days refers to new-grain מצה, which is allowed after the עומר on the 16th of ניסן. This proves when the עומר is brought.

steps.title: Can the counting start whenever one wants?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא suggests a first possible reading: harvest and bring the עומר on time, but begin counting whenever you like.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says "From the day that you bring... you shall count." Maybe this means you harvest and bring the עומר, and then you count whenever you want?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to a new question: when exactly the count of the עומר must begin. It raises a possible mistaken reading so that it can correct it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ויקרא connects counting to the day of bringing the עומר, but it does not clearly say the count must start right away. So one might think only the harvesting and bringing have a fixed time, and the counting is flexible.

keyTerms.meaning: "One might think": the opening of a possible reading that the ברייתא will reject
Whenever he wants
The barley offering brought on the second day of פסח
You shall count

phrases.english: "From the day that you bring ... you shall count"
One might think he should harvest and bring [the עומר],
and count whenever he wants?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל יִקְצוֹר וְיָבִיא, וְאֵימָתַי שֶׁיִּרְצֶה יִסְפּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 7 set the עומר on the second day of פסח. Now the ברייתא asks when the counting must start.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the counting have to begin at a fixed time, or can it start whenever one wants?

steps.title: The counting starts with the harvest
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in דברים ties the start of the count to the moment the harvesting begins.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק teaches: "From when the sickle is first put to the standing grain, you shall begin to count."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers the question by bringing a second פסוק. It shows the counting starts right when the harvest starts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in דברים says the count begins "from when the sickle is first put" to the grain. So the counting is not flexible. It is fixed to the harvest of the עומר.

keyTerms.meaning: "The פסוק teaches": a source is brought to decide the question
Sickle
Standing grain that has not been cut yet
From when it begins

phrases.english: The verse teaches:
"From when the sickle is first put to the standing grain
you shall begin to count."
phrases.notes: דברים 16:9

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״מֵהָחֵל חֶרְמֵשׁ בַּקָּמָה תָּחֵל לִסְפֹּר״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The counting must begin when the harvesting begins.

steps.title: Then maybe the bringing can be whenever one wants
steps.stepSummary: If we had only the harvest פסוק, one might think the bringing of the עומר is flexible.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we only had "From when the sickle is first put... begin to count," one might think you harvest and count, and bring the עומר whenever you want.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now pushes on the answer it just gave. If only the harvest is tied to the count, maybe the bringing has no fixed time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in דברים fixed the count to the harvest, but it says nothing about bringing the עומר. So a new gap opens: maybe the bringing can be delayed.

keyTerms.meaning: If: "if we only had this פסוק"
He harvests
He counts
He brings the offering

phrases.english: If [we only had] "From when the sickle is first put... you shall begin to count,"
one might think he should harvest and count,
and bring whenever he wants?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי ״מֵהָחֵל חֶרְמֵשׁ תָּחֵל לִסְפּוֹר״ – יָכוֹל יִקְצוֹר וְיִסְפּוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes on the answer of step 9 by showing what it leaves open.
steps.kashyaTarget: Relying only on the פסוק in דברים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That פסוק ties the count to the harvest but sets no time for bringing the עומר.

steps.title: The count is also tied to the bringing
steps.stepSummary: The first פסוק, "from the day that you bring," shows the bringing is also linked to the start of the count.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק teaches: "From the day that you bring."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא goes back to the פסוק from ויקרא to close the gap. The bringing is also tied to the day the counting starts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now both פסוקים work together. דברים links the count to the harvest, and ויקרא links the count to the bringing. So neither the harvest nor the bringing can be moved.

keyTerms.meaning: "From the day that you bring": the count is tied to the day of bringing the עומר

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "From the day that you bring."

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״מִיּוֹם הֲבִיאֲכֶם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Bringing a second פסוק to cover what the first one leaves open
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The bringing of the עומר could be at any time.
steps.terutzMaskana: The bringing is tied to the start of the count, just like the harvest.

steps.title: Then maybe everything happens in the daytime
steps.stepSummary: Because the פסוק says "day," one might think harvesting, counting and bringing all happen in the daytime.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we go by "From the day that you bring," one might think he harvests, counts and brings all during the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a new problem. The word "day" in the פסוק could suggest that all three actions must be done in the daytime.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question has moved from "which day" to "what time of day." The word ״יום״ might mean daytime, not night.

keyTerms.meaning: In the daytime
Day: here the question is whether it means daytime as opposed to night

phrases.english: If [we go by] "From the day that you bring,"
one might think he should harvest, count and bring during the day?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי ״מִיּוֹם הֲבִיאֲכֶם״ – יָכוֹל יִקְצוֹר וְיִסְפּוֹר וְיָבִיא בַּיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the פסוק used in step 11 and shows a new possible misreading of it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If "day" means daytime, then all the actions, including counting, should be done by day.

steps.title: Complete weeks means counting from the evening
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק requires seven complete weeks, and that only works if the counting starts at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק teaches: "Seven complete weeks there shall be." When are there seven complete weeks? When you start counting from the evening.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with another phrase from the same פסוק. It shows the counting must start at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Jewish day begins at night. If you start counting in the daytime, you already missed the first night, so the weeks would not be complete. Starting at night makes the seven weeks full.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: weeks
Complete, whole
To count
From the evening

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with steps 3–5. There the question was what ״השבת״ means. Here ״שֶׁבַע שַׁבָּתוֹת״ simply means seven weeks.

phrases.english: The verse teaches
"Seven complete weeks there shall be."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 23:15

phrases.english: When do you find
seven complete weeks?
When you start counting from the evening.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״שֶׁבַע שַׁבָּתוֹת תְּמִימֹת תִּהְיֶינָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reasoning from another word in the פסוק ("complete")
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everything, including counting, is done in the daytime.
steps.terutzMaskana: Counting must begin at night so the weeks are complete.

steps.title: Then maybe everything happens at night
steps.stepSummary: Now that counting begins at night, one might think harvesting and bringing also happen at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think he should harvest, bring and count all at night?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא swings the other way. If counting is at night, maybe all three actions are at night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13 moved the counting to night. The new question is whether the harvesting and bringing simply follow the counting.

keyTerms.meaning: At night

phrases.english: One might think he should harvest, bring and count at night?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל יִקְצוֹר וְיָבִיא וְיִסְפּוֹר בַּלַּיְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the answer of step 13 too far, to everything at night.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that counting begins at night
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If counting is at night, perhaps the whole עומר process, bringing included, is at night.

steps.title: Harvest and count at night, bring in the day
steps.stepSummary: "From the day that you bring" shows the bringing is by day. The final rule: harvesting and counting at night, bringing in the day.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק teaches: "From the day that you bring." So how does it work? The harvesting and the counting are at night, and the bringing is in the day.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא uses "day" once more to show the bringing is by day. Then it combines everything into one final rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase gets its job. "Complete weeks" puts the counting, and with it the harvest, at night. "From the day that you bring" puts the bringing in the day. The ברייתא combines them into one rule.

keyTerms.meaning: "How so?": how do we fit the פסוקים together?
Harvesting
Counting
Bringing the offering

steps.whatToRemember: The עומר is harvested at night and the counting starts at night, on the night of the second day of פסח. The עומר itself is brought in the daytime.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is why ספירת העומר begins at night, at the start of the second day of פסח.

phrases.english: The verse teaches: "From the day that you bring."
So how does it work?
Harvesting and counting are at night,
and bringing is in the day.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָא כֵּיצַד? קְצִירָה וּסְפִירָה בַּלַּיְלָה, וַהֲבָאָה בַּיּוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 14 and closes the whole series with one rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Harvesting the עומר and counting happen at night. Bringing the עומר happens in the daytime.

steps.title: רבא says almost every proof can be pushed off
steps.stepSummary: רבא says every proof can be pushed off except the proofs of the last two תנאים in each ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: All of them can be pushed off, except for the last two תנאים, both in the first ברייתא and in the second ברייתא. Those cannot be pushed off.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא looks back at all the proofs the גמרא brought against the בייתוסים and gives a general verdict. This sets up the next steps, where he shows how each weaker proof can be pushed off.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the proofs were simply listed one after another. רבא sorts them. Most of them can be answered, but the last two תנאים in each ברייתא give proofs that truly stand.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation; a way to push off a proof
The last תנאים quoted in a list
The first ברייתא
The last (second) ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not saying the בייתוסים are right. Everyone agrees the count starts on the second day of פסח. He is only asking which proofs for that are strong.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: כּוּלְּהוּ אִית לְהוּ פִּירְכָא,
phrases.english: Rava said: All of them have a refutation,
phrases.notes: "All of them" means all the proofs from the two ברייתות against the בייתוסים.

phrases.english: except for the two last tanna'im,
both in the first baraita
and in the last baraita,
for which there is no refutation.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: כּוּלְּהוּ אִית לְהוּ פִּירְכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the details of harvesting, counting and bringing the עומר back to judging the proofs against the בייתוסים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every proof can be pushed off except those of the last two תנאים in each ברייתא.

steps.title: Pushing off the proof of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי
steps.stepSummary: The clash between counting days and counting weeks can be solved by saying we count both, as אביי says.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want a proof from רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, maybe the answer is like אביי. אביי said: There is a מצוה to count days, and there is a מצוה to count weeks.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא shows why the proof of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי is not a real proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן יוחנן בן זכאי pointed to two פסוקים that seem to clash. One says to count fifty days and one says to count weeks. He settled the clash in a way that only works if the count starts from יום טוב, so the clash became his proof. רבא says the clash can be settled another way: following אביי, we count both the days and the weeks. So the clash does not prove when the count starts.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps; used to suggest a different way to explain
A מצוה to count the days
A מצוה to count the weeks

steps.whyThisMatters: אביי's rule is why we count both days and weeks each night, for example "today is eight days, which is one week and one day."

phrases.english: If from that of Rabban Yoḥanan ben Zakkai,
phrases.notes: He means: if you want to prove it from what רבן יוחנן בן זכאי said, that the פסוקים about days and weeks seem to clash.

phrases.english: perhaps it is in accordance with Abaye,
as Abaye said:
It is a מצוה to count days,
and it is a מצוה to count weeks.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִדְּרַבָּן יוֹחָנָן בֶּן זַכַּאי, דִּלְמָא כִּדְאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first example of a proof that, as רבא said, can be pushed off.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof of רבן יוחנן בן זכאי from the clash between counting days and counting weeks.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The clash is solved by counting both days and weeks, as אביי says, so it does not show when the count starts.

steps.title: Pushing off the proofs of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: Even if their proofs show the count starts after יום טוב, maybe it means the last day of פסח, not the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want a proof from רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע: how do we know it means the first day of יום טוב? Maybe it means the last day of יום טוב!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא shows why the proofs of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע are not enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their proofs show that the word "שבת" in the פסוק means יום טוב and not a regular Saturday. But פסח has two ימים טובים, the first day and the seventh day. Their proofs do not tell us which one, so the count could start after the last day.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know?
The first day of פסח
The last (seventh) day of פסח
It refers to; it is talking about

phrases.english: If from that of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Yehoshua,
from where do we know that it is referring to the first day of the Festival?
Perhaps it is referring to the last day of the Festival!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִדְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, מִמַּאי דִּבְיוֹם טוֹב רִאשׁוֹן קָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second example of proofs that can be pushed off.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proofs of רבי אליעזר and רבי יהושע that the count starts after יום טוב.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: They show the count starts after a יום טוב, but not which one. It could be the seventh day of פסח.

steps.title: The proofs of רבי ישמעאל and רבי יהודה בן בתירא stand
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the proofs of רבי ישמעאל and רבי יהודה בן בתירא cannot be pushed off.
steps.simpleTranslation: The proofs of רבי ישמעאל and רבי יהודה בן בתירא have no refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא names the last two תנאים of the first ברייתא and says their proofs are solid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After pushing off the weaker proofs, רבא points to the strong ones. רבי ישמעאל brought a proof from the שתי הלחם, which are brought at the start of a יום טוב. רבי יהודה בן בתירא brought a proof from the word "שבת" used about שבועות. These proofs show the count must start right after the first day of פסח.

keyTerms.meaning: They have no refutation; the proof stands
Counting the עומר, the fifty days from פסח to שבועות
"From the day after the שבת"; the פסוק the whole debate is about

steps.whatToRemember: Many proofs were brought against the בייתוסים, but רבא says the strong ones are those of the last תנאים, like רבי ישמעאל and רבי יהודה בן בתירא. The others can be explained another way.

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא –
phrases.english: That of Rabbi Yishmael and Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira
have no refutation.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא לֵית לְהוּ פִּירְכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After pushing off the weaker proofs, רבא names the proofs that stand.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The proofs of רבי ישמעאל and רבי יהודה בן בתירא cannot be pushed off. They firmly show the count starts after the first day of פסח.

steps.title: Pushing off the proof of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: רבא shows that the proof of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה can be answered: maybe the פסוק means fifty days not counting the six extra ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want to prove it from רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, I could answer: maybe the Torah means fifty days, not counting these six extra days.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא is pushing off the first proof in the second ברייתא, the one from רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה argued that if counting starts after a regular שבת, the gap between one year's start and the next could be 50 to 56 days, which does not fit 'fifty days.' רבא answers that the 'fifty' could mean fifty counted days, with the extra six days simply not counted. So this proof does not force the conclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps, maybe
Fifty
Besides, not counting
Six

phrases.english: If from Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda,
I would say:
perhaps it means fifty, besides these six.
phrases.notes: 'These six' are the up-to-six extra days that could come out between the years.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִדְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה הֲוָה אָמֵינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues רבא's list of push-offs, now in the second ברייתא
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, not his conclusion
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word 'fifty' could mean fifty counted days, with the six extra days not counted

steps.title: Pushing off the proof of רבי יהודה בן בתירא
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers רבי יהודה בן בתירא's proof: even if the count depends on the court's calendar, maybe it starts after the last day of יום טוב, not the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want to prove it from רבי יהודה בן בתירא: how do you know it means the first day of יום טוב? Maybe it means the last day of יום טוב!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes off the second proof in this ברייתא, from רבי יהודה בן בתירא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה בן בתירא showed that the counting depends on the court, so it must start from a day the court sets, like יום טוב, not a weekly שבת. רבא answers that the last day of פסח is also set by the court. So this proof does not show the count starts right after the first day.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know?
It is referring to, it stands on
The first day of פסח
The last (seventh) day of פסח

phrases.english: If from Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira,
from where do we know that it refers to the first day of יום טוב?
Perhaps it refers to the last day of יום טוב!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מִדְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתֵירָא מִמַּאי דִּבְיוֹם טוֹב רִאשׁוֹן קָאֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The same kind of push-off used in step 18, now applied to רבי יהודה בן בתירא's proof in the second ברייתא
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof of רבי יהודה בן בתירא in the second ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Something set by the court could also be the last day of פסח, not only the first

steps.title: רבי יוסי himself saw a weakness in his first proof
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that רבי יוסי knew his first proof could be answered, which is why he added 'ועוד' with a second proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוסי also saw that his first proof could be answered, and that is why he said 'and furthermore.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains why he does not need to push off רבי יוסי's first proof himself: רבי יוסי already showed he saw a problem with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי first argued that from a regular שבת we would not know which שבת is meant. Then he said 'ועוד' and gave a second proof. That 'ועוד' shows he felt the first proof was weak, so only his second proof and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's proof remain unanswered.

keyTerms.meaning: Sees
A refutation, a weak point in a proof
And furthermore; adding another proof

steps.whatToRemember: In the second ברייתא, the first proofs can all be pushed off. Only the last two, רבי יוסי's second proof and רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's proof, stand without an answer, just as רבא said.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי נָמֵי חָזֵי לֵיהּ פִּירְכָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yosei too saw a refutation for it,
phrases.notes: 'It' is his first proof, that after a regular שבת we wouldn't know which שבת is meant.

phrases.english: and that is why he said "and furthermore."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹסֵי נָמֵי חָזֵי לֵיהּ פִּירְכָא וְהַיְינוּ דְּקָאָמַר וְעוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבא's push-offs in the second ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רבי יוסי's own word 'ועוד' shows he knew the first proof was not strong enough

steps.title: אביי: count both days and weeks
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to אביי's statement: there is a מצוה to count the days and a מצוה to count the weeks.
steps.simpleTranslation: Back to the statement itself: אביי said, it is a מצוה to count days, and it is a מצוה to count weeks.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to look closely at אביי's rule, which was quoted earlier during the discussion of the proofs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier (step 17) אביי's rule was used to solve a clash between 'count fifty days' and 'count seven weeks.' Now the גמרא brings it up on its own as a practical rule: when counting the עומר, you mention both the days and the weeks.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter itself'; returning to examine a statement quoted earlier
A commandment
To count
Days
Weeks

phrases.english: The matter itself:
phrases.notes: The גמרא is going back to אביי's rule, which came up earlier as a side point.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
It is a מצוה to count days,
and it is a מצוה to count weeks.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section examining a statement quoted in step 17
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a מצוה to count both the days and the weeks of the עומר

steps.title: How the Sages actually counted: both, or days only
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים of רב אשי's study hall counted days and weeks; אמימר counted only days, because today the count is only a זכר למקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים of רב אשי's study hall counted days and counted weeks. אמימר counted days but not weeks. He said: it is only a remembrance of the בית המקדש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports how different חכמים actually practiced אביי's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי's study hall followed אביי fully and counted both. אמימר counted only days, explaining that with no עומר offering today, the counting is only a זכר למקדש. So he did not feel he needed to do both parts.

keyTerms.meaning: They counted
A remembrance of the בית המקדש

steps.whatToRemember: אביי says count both days and weeks. רב אשי's study hall did both, while אמימר counted only days, because without the בית המקדש the count is a זכר למקדש.
steps.confusionAlert: אמימר is not saying the counting today is meaningless or that weeks are never counted. He is saying that, since it is only a זכר למקדש, counting the days alone is enough.

phrases.english: The Sages of the study hall of Rav Ashi
counted days and counted weeks;
Ameimar counted days
and did not count weeks.
He said: it is a remembrance of the Temple.
phrases.notes: He means that since there is no עומר offering today, the count is only to remember the בית המקדש.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּנַן דְּבֵי רַב אָשֵׁי מָנוּ יוֹמֵי וּמָנוּ שָׁבוּעֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how אביי's rule from step 23 was actually practiced
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב אשי's study hall counted both days and weeks; אמימר counted only days, since today the count is a זכר למקדש

steps.title: Bringing the עומר and singeing it on the stalks
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that after cutting the עומר, they put it in baskets and brought it to the עזרה. According to רבי מאיר, they singed it in fire while still on the stalk to fulfill the מצוה of קלי.
steps.simpleTranslation: After they cut the עומר, they put it into baskets and brought it to the Temple courtyard. They would singe it in the fire to fulfill the מצוה of parched grain. This is the view of רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins and describes what was done with the עומר barley right after it was cut. רבי מאיר says it was singed in the fire while still on the stalks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה requires the עומר grain to be 'parched' (קלי). רבי מאיר holds that this parching happened by passing the stalks, with the kernels still on them, through fire. The next line will show that the חכמים disagree about how the kernels were handled.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה; the text of the משנה being studied
Baskets
The courtyard of the בית המקדש
Singeing; passing something lightly through fire
The מצוה that the עומר grain must be parched

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
They harvested it and placed it in baskets,
phrases.notes: 'It' here means the עומר barley that was just cut.

phrases.english: they brought it to the Temple courtyard,
and they would singe it in the fire,
in order to fulfill with it the מצוה of parched grain,
these are the words of Rabbi Meir.

steps.triggerLanguage: קְצָרוּהוּ וּנְתָנוּהוּ בְּקוּפּוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, moving on from the discussion of counting the עומר to how the עומר itself was prepared.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי מאיר, the עומר was singed in fire while still on the stalks, to fulfill the מצוה of קלי.

steps.title: The חכמים: beat the kernels off with soft reeds
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say the kernels were beaten off the stalks with reeds and cabbage stalks, so that they would not be crushed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים say: they beat it with reeds and cabbage stalks, so that it would not get crushed.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים give their view, which disagrees with רבי מאיר. They say the kernels were first knocked off the stalks with soft tools.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, the first step is to remove the kernels from the stalks, not to singe them on the stalk. They used soft, moist reeds and cabbage stalks rather than hard sticks, so the delicate fresh kernels would not get crushed.

keyTerms.meaning: Reeds
Cabbage stalks
Beating or threshing
Get crushed or squashed

phrases.english: And the Rabbis say:
with reeds and with cabbage stalks they beat it,
so that it would not be crushed.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing view to רבי מאיר in the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, the kernels were first beaten off the stalks with soft reeds and cabbage stalks so they would not be crushed.

steps.title: Parching in a holed pan and cooling in the wind
steps.stepSummary: The kernels were put in a perforated pan so the fire could reach all of them. Afterward they were spread out in the עזרה for the wind to blow on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: They put it into a pan, and the pan had holes in it, so the fire could reach all of it. Then they spread it out in the courtyard, and the wind blew on it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues describing the steps. The kernels are parched in a pan with holes, then spread out to cool and dry in the wind.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The holes in the pan let the fire touch every kernel, so all of the grain is properly parched. Spreading the kernels out afterward lets the wind cool and dry them before they are ground.

keyTerms.meaning: A hollow pan or tube used for parching
Full of holes; perforated
Takes hold of; reaches
They spread it out

phrases.english: They placed it into a hollow vessel,
and the vessel was perforated,
so that the fire would take hold of all of it.
They spread it out in the courtyard,
and the wind blows on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְתָנוּהוּ לְאַבּוּב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the step-by-step process in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The kernels were parched in a perforated pan so the fire reached all of them, then spread out in the עזרה to cool in the wind.

steps.title: Grinding, sifting the עשרון, and the leftover flour
steps.stepSummary: The grain was ground coarsely, and one עשרון was taken out after being sifted through thirteen sifters. The rest was redeemed and could be eaten by anyone. It is obligated in חלה and exempt from מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: They put it into a mill for coarse grinding and took out one tenth of an איפה of flour, sifted through thirteen sifters. The rest is redeemed and may be eaten by anyone. It is obligated in חלה and exempt from מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes the process. Only one עשרון of very fine flour goes to the קרבן, and it also rules on what happens to all the leftover flour.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Much more barley was cut than was needed. Only one עשרון, sifted thirteen times, was used for the קרבן. The leftover flour was still holy, so it had to be redeemed before regular people could eat it. Once redeemed, dough made from it needs חלה taken, but it is free from מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: A mill that grinds coarsely, into grits
One tenth of an איפה, the measure of flour for the עומר
A sifter or sieve
Is redeemed, taken out of holiness by paying its value
The portion of dough that must be given to a כהן
Tithe, the tenth of produce that must be separated

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the leftover flour was part of the קרבן. Only the one sifted עשרון was offered; the rest was simply redeemed and eaten like regular food.

phrases.english: They placed it in a mill of grits,
and they took out from it a tenth of an ephah,
which is sifted through thirteen sifters,
and the rest is redeemed and eaten by any person,
and it is obligated in challa,
phrases.notes: 'It' here is dough made from the leftover flour.

phrases.english: and it is exempt from the tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: נְתָנוּהוּ לְרֵיחַיִם שֶׁל גָּרוֹסוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the process and adds rulings on the leftover flour.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One עשרון sifted through thirteen sifters is offered. The rest is redeemed and eaten by anyone; it is obligated in חלה and exempt from מעשר.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: obligated in מעשרות too
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא disagrees and says the leftover flour is obligated in both חלה and מעשרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says it is obligated in חלה and in מעשרות.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא disagrees with the end of the משנה. He says the leftover flour is not exempt from מעשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees that the leftover flour needs חלה. The argument is only about מעשר: the first view exempts it, and רבי עקיבא obligates it.

keyTerms.meaning: Holds that it is obligated
Tithes (plural)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה has two arguments. רבי מאיר and the חכמים argue about how the grain was first parched. The first view and רבי עקיבא argue about whether the leftover flour needs מעשר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva deems it obligated in challa and in tithes.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא מְחַיֵּיב בַּחַלָּה וּבַמַּעַשְׂרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the ruling in the previous step that the leftover flour is exempt from מעשר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי עקיבא, the leftover flour is obligated in both חלה and מעשרות.

steps.title: A ברייתא brings the פסוק for רבי מאיר's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that reads 'אביב קלוי באש' as teaching that the grain was singed in fire to fulfill the מצוה of קלי, according to רבי מאיר. It then begins the view of the חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'אביב' means fresh grain. 'קלוי באש' teaches that the Jewish people would singe it in fire to fulfill the מצוה of parched grain. This is the view of רבי מאיר. And the חכמים say:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins by quoting a ברייתא that shows where the מחלוקת in the משנה comes from in the פסוק. This step sets up the next move: the חכמים' reading, which starts right here and continues in the next part of the text.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the grain must be 'קלוי באש', parched in fire. רבי מאיר learns from this that the grain was singed in fire to fulfill the מצוה of קלי. The ברייתא has just started the חכמים' reading of the same פסוק, which will explain their different view.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion of the אמוראים on the משנה
A teaching of the תנאים that is not in the משנה
Fresh, ripe grain in the ear
Parched in fire
It teaches; introduces what the פסוק is coming to teach
